description: Collective-intelligence surveys — taking a survey the back end holds and recording the response: the ideas chosen in priority order plus one new idea that was not in the set. A program names the survey with `id "…"`; its ideas, title, instructions and bounds come from the survey itself and CANNOT be written in code. A survey with several versions draws one per session. L0182 describes no flow and has no interactive player.

example_prompts.prompt: Answer the you-can-choose survey for me — I pick whichever two ideas you think matter most.
example_prompts.notes: The ordinary request: a survey exists and what is brought to it is an answer. `survey [id "you-can-choose" session-id get-val-public "itemId" response [...]]` — the ideas come back from the survey, and the program never writes them.

example_prompts.prompt: Answer the team-retro survey with cutting the build time in half first, then the flaky tests.
example_prompts.notes: `selection` names the ideas chosen and the order IS the ranking. Name each by its exact text — the ideas live in the survey, so the ids cannot be known when the response is written.

example_prompts.prompt: Add my own idea alongside my selection: make public transit free.
example_prompts.notes: `idea` must not repeat one already in the set — that is what makes it new.

example_prompts.prompt: Record just a new idea — I do not want to pick any of the existing ones.
example_prompts.notes: `idea` may stand alone; `selection` comes back empty, where the survey's floor allows it.

example_prompts.prompt: Reorder my selection so the housing idea comes first.
example_prompts.notes: Reordering `selection` IS re-ranking; there is no separate rank step.
you-can-choose, team-retro, city-budget, product-features and school. An id that does not exist is a compile error naming the ones that do.

example_prompts.prompt: Take version 7 of you-can-choose rather than whichever one it gives me.
example_prompts.notes: `id "you-can-choose-7"` takes that version outright, with no draw. The version drawn for a session is in `instance` in the compiled record.

example_prompts.prompt: Set up a survey asking my team what to fix first, with these eight ideas.
example_prompts.notes: NOT possible here. A survey's ideas, wording and bounds belong to the back end, and no word writes them; L0182 only takes surveys that already exist.
